title: A choice on every turn
idea: TOOL: weave a decision into a loop - branch per item to count, total, or skip.

exercises.prompt: You loop over items and want to treat some differently from others. What thread adds that?
exercises.explanation: An if inside the loop makes a per-item choice - include it, skip it, or handle it differently. Choice woven into a repeat.
8, 5, and 10 are > 4, so kept rises to 3. The if chooses which items to count each turn.

exercises.prompt: The if inside a loop runs once per item, deciding that item's fate.
exercises.explanation: True. Each turn, the condition is tested on the current item, and the matching branch runs. A choice per repeat.
Count items LESS than 10: n < 10. That's 4 and 9, so kept = 2.
Three 1s (hits) and one 0 (miss). if/else routes each shot to one counter - a choice plus multiple state.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a loop that counts even numbers (n % 2 == 0).
exercises.explanation: Start the counter, loop, test each n for evenness, count it, print. 4 and 10 are even, so evens = 2.

exercises.prompt: In a loop, what's the difference between putting an update INSIDE vs OUTSIDE the if?
options: Inside runs only for matching items; outside runs for every item
exercises.explanation: Placement decides scope. Inside the if = conditional (some items); outside = unconditional (all items). Choose on purpose.

exercises.prompt: Weaving a decision into a loop lets you count, total, or skip items selectively.
exercises.explanation: True. The if picks which items affect your running values. Filter, grouped counts, and conditional totals all come from this weave.
No item passes the test, so the body never runs and kept stays 0. The choice correctly excludes everything.

options: A decision inside a loop makes a per-item choice
exercises.explanation: Choice-in-a-repeat is one of the most common integrations - the heart of filtering and grouping.
